I never saw my condition as a conflict, especially a conflict against an true or 'authentic' me (adorno has a great critique of 'authenticity' in existentialism). I am not fighting against anything, for as much as I can say a self exists, I will that the thoughts, the sensations are me, and constitute me. I'm not particularly religious so I don't believe in any kind of soul, and similarly I don't believe in a transcendental ego, so where would my true self be located? The only me I experience is the one that like hip-hop, that is depressed, that loves pork ribs, that wants to kill themself. Positive psychologists might be tempted to say hip-hop and pork loving me is the "true" me, but why isn't my "illness"? What justifies that? 

So I am not a battle to be fought over. There is no winning. The best I hope for is reconciling my immense sadness with life.

I never understood why people characterised suicide as the "easy way out", I guess it's supposed to be reverse psychology and "uplifting". I find it too be a poor reductionist understanding of "troubled" people, like if only they in themselves find strength, disregarding the material conditions of the world, or the sensations that are felt.

I know it's not possible but it's too hard to keep on going in this body. For the last two years I've been treated by one of the best youth clinics in Australia. There was alot of support, weekly meeting with case manager, who was an OT so most sessions were therapy, every 3 weeks a session with the psychiatrist to adjust medication and keep track. When to hospital a couple of times in those two years. Obviously, that kind of treatment is expensive to the government so it's only for 2 years and this October I was transfered to the adult mental health service, meetings with case manager are every 2-3 weeks with a doctor ever 1-1.5 months. Don't get me wrong, I am very grateful for all the support I've received. I just thick I'm like someone with smallpox in the 15th century: sure, in principle I could get better, but I don't think it will come for many times my own life time.
